items: **Blue Water Policy:** associated with **Francisco de Almeida**; its aim was Portuguese naval/trade (trading) supremacy in the Indian Ocean.

parts.t: English factories and forts in Andhra and Madras
items: **Machilipatnam, 1611:** the first factory by the English at Machilipatnam was set up by the English East India Company in 1611, with permission by **Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah**.

lectures.title: Struggle for supremacy in Bengal: Plassey and Buxar

items: **First major territorial base** of the East India Company: Bengal.
**Bengal's trade in the 18th century:** cotton, silk, saltpetre and opium exports.
**Opponents:** British vs Siraj-ud-daula (Robert Clive vs Siraj-ud-Daulah).
**Leader / commander:** **Robert Clive**, who is associated with the Battle of Plassey.
**Result:** British control over Bengal established; the battle is associated with treachery.
**Plassey (1757)** is the beginning of British supremacy.

parts.t: Battle of Buxar, 1764, and the Treaty of Allahabad
items: **Opponents:** British vs the allied forces of Mir Qasim + Shuja-ud-Daula + Shah Alam II.
**Commander:** Major **Hector Munro** defeated the allied forces.
**Result:** a major British victory; a more decisive consolidation of British supremacy.
**Treaty of Allahabad, 1765:** Robert Clive – Shah Alam II / Shuja-ud-Daula; made after the Battle of Buxar.

lectures.title: Struggle for supremacy: the Marathas and the British

items: **3rd Battle of Panipat, 1761:** the invader Ahmad Shah Abdali / Durrani (target: North India) defeated the Marathas; a major setback to Maratha expansion.
**Battle of Kharda / Khurda, 1795:** Marathas vs Nizam; the Nizam was defeated by the Marathas (a Maratha victory).

**Opponents:** Muzaffar Jang (Jung) + Chanda Sahib + French vs Anwar-ud-din.
**Result:** Anwar-ud-din was defeated and killed; Chanda Sahib gained control of the Carnatic.
**Place in the wars:** part of the 2nd Carnatic War.
**Opponents:** British vs French: British forces under **Sir Eyre Coote** vs Count (de) Lally's French forces.
**Result:** British victory; Count de Lally was defeated.
**Wandiwash (1760)** was decisive in the 3rd Carnatic War.

parts.t: Warren Hastings and the early institutions
items: **Warren Hastings:** associated with the Regulating Act and the Ring Fence policy.
**Ring Fence Policy:** buffer states to protect Company territories.
**Calcutta Madarsa:** founded by Warren Hastings at Calcutta in 1780; the first Madarsa set up by the British in India. Warren Hastings is associated with Oriental education.
**Sanskrit College, Banaras:** founded by **Jonathan Duncan** at Varanasi / Banaras in 1791; the first Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya at Varanasi/Banaras.
**Cornwallis:** associated with the Permanent Settlement and the Cornwallis Code.
**Subsidiary Alliance:** associated with Lord **Wellesley**; its purpose was to bring Indian states under British political/military control.
**William Bentinck:** abolition of Sati; the first Governor-General of India.

parts.t: Dalhousie: Doctrine of Lapse and annexations
items: **Doctrine of Lapse:** associated with Lord **Dalhousie**; annexation of states where the ruler died without a natural (male) heir.
**Dalhousie** is associated with the Doctrine of Lapse and with railways/telegraph.
**Punjab / Sikh Empire, 1849:** annexed by the British after the 2nd Anglo-Sikh War; associated with Lord Dalhousie; **Duleep Singh** = last Sikh ruler.
**Railway development, official reasons:** faster movement, communication, administration, troop movement.
**Railway development, colonial economic purpose:** raw materials → ports; British goods → Indian markets.
